info.title: OpenID Conformance Suite REST APIs
info.description:
The REST APIs for driving the OpenID Conformance Suite.

Authentication

To call the APIs supply a bearer token, which can be either:
  • an API token obtained from the token management page (full access, scoped to the token's owner), or
  • a share-link JWT issued by POST /api/info/{testId}/share or POST /api/plan/{id}/share (read-only access scoped to the shared plan and its tests).

Typical workflow

Most users want to run a test plan and collect its results:
  1. Find the plan to run, its variants and its configuration fields: GET /api/plan/available. (Tip: after creating the plan once in the web UI, GET /api/lastconfig returns the plan name, variant selection and configuration JSON needed for the next step.)
  2. Create a plan instance: POST /api/plan?planName=...&variant=... with the configuration JSON. The response contains the plan id and the list of modules to run.
  3. For each module, create a test instance with POST /api/runner?test={testModule}&plan={planId}, then wait for it to finish with GET /api/runner/{id}/wait-state (or by polling GET /api/info/{id}). A test in the WAITING state needs interaction: GET /api/runner/{id} lists any front-channel URLs to visit.
  4. Read the outcome from GET /api/info/{id} (status and result) and the detailed log from GET /api/log/{id}.
  5. Download the plan's results with GET /api/plan/exporthtml/{id}, or prepare a certification package with POST /api/plan/{id}/certificationpackage.
The run-test-plan.py script implements this whole flow (it is what our own CI uses) and adds functionality like suppressing known failures; the tutorial linked below shows how to use it.

The raw OpenAPI document behind this page can be fed to an OpenAPI client generator.

get.summary: Get a list of test plan instances with paging
get.description:
Which plans are listed is decided by who is asking: an admin sees every plan, anyone else sees their own, and `public=true` lists the published plans. The optional filters below only narrow that listing - the statistics page drills down with them - so none of them can show a plan that would not have been listed anyway.

In addition to the parameters below, any number of plan level variant filters may be sent as `variant.<parameter>=<value>`, e.g. `variant.fapi_profile=openbanking_brazil&variant.client_auth_type=mtls`; a plan has to match all of them. They cannot be declared individually here because the parameter names are the variant parameters of every test plan the suite publishes.

delete.summary: Delete every plan a filtered listing shows, and their tests and logs (admin only)
delete.description:
Takes exactly the parameters `GET /api/plan` takes and deletes what that listing would show, so the way to see what this will do is to list it first. Deleting millions of documents is far too long for a request, so the work runs in the background: this returns 202 and `GET /api/plan/delete-status` reports progress.

Two kinds of plan are never deleted, whatever is asked for: one a certification package has been downloaded for (`immutable`), and one that has been published, since a link to it may be in circulation. They are left out of the count as well as of the deleting.

Refused unless at least one filter is present - there is no way to ask this to delete everything - and unless `confirm` is the number of plans it is about to delete, so that a listing that has changed since it was looked at stops the request rather than deleting something else.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Delete at most this many plans, oldest first. Omit to delete all of them.

parameters.name: confirm
parameters.description: The number of plans this will delete, as a check that it is what was seen

get.summary: Get suite-wide usage statistics across all users (admin only)
get.description:
Served from a snapshot that is recomputed in the background at most every 12 hours, because the underlying aggregations group over the whole test database. While the first snapshot is being computed the response is 202 and the client should poll. The filters and the range are applied to that snapshot when the request is answered, so they are free to change and never trigger a recomputation.

In addition to the parameters below, any number of plan level variant filters may be sent as `variant.<parameter>=<value>`, e.g. `variant.fapi_profile=openbanking_brazil&variant.client_auth_type=mtls`; a cell has to match all of them. They cannot be declared individually here because the parameter names are the variant parameters of every test plan the suite publishes.

`data.modules` covers the trailing 24 months only, is clipped to the range by month whatever the granularity, and honours `family` and `plan` as registry membership - a module belongs to every family that has a plan running it. The `variant.<parameter>` and `cert` filters do not apply to it: a test run records neither in a form the module counts can be keyed by. Its `runs` counts only runs by an identified user, since the section counts people and a run written before authentication completed belongs to nobody, so it does not reconcile exactly with the runs charts.

`data.heatmap` and `data.externalHosts` cover the trailing 24 months, and the summary tiles are windowed too: `inProgress` and `stuck` count runs of the last year, `totalTests` is the run collection's own document count (an estimate to within a few documents) and `totalUsers` counts users who created a test plan, so somebody who has only ever run standalone tests is not in it. Everything else is all time.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: Recompute the snapshot even if the current one is still fresh; any existing snapshot keeps being served meanwhile

parameters.name: granularity
parameters.description: The time buckets to report in. Monthly covers the whole history; weekly covers the trailing 104 weeks and is keyed by the Monday of each ISO week.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first period to report, inclusive; `YYYY-MM` for monthly, `YYYY-MM-DD` for weekly (any day of the week, snapped to its Monday). Defaults to as far back as there is data.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The last period to report, inclusive, in the same format as `from`. Defaults to today.

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: Only count test plans of this spec family, as named in the `families` list of the response.

parameters.name: plan
parameters.description: Only count this test plan, by name, as listed in `dimensions.plans`.

parameters.name: cert
parameters.description: Only count test plans whose certification profiles are exactly this, as listed in `dimensions.certProfiles`; several profiles are joined with ' | '.

get.summary: The families and plan names a listing can be narrowed to
get.description:
What `GET /api/plan`'s `family` and `plan` parameters accept, so that they can be offered rather than typed. Plan names include the ones the suite no longer publishes - a listing of old plans is mostly made of those, and they are exactly what somebody clearing a database out is looking for - each marked `retired`.

Deliberately not `/api/plan/available`, which answers the same question but carries every plan's modules, variants and configuration fields with it: 680 KB against this one's few.

Readable on a public request (`?public=true`) as well as by a logged in user: this is the plan registry, the same material `/api/plan/available` already answers with on one, and holds nothing about anybody's data. Pinned by `scripts/run-security-tests.py`.

get.summary: Get test log of given testId
get.description: Returns the raw log entries sorted by time. Every entry has _id, testId, testOwner, src (the logging component, e.g. a condition class name) and time (milliseconds since the epoch); most carry msg, and common further keys include result (SUCCESS/FAILURE/WARNING/INFO/REVIEW), requirements (spec references), blockId, img/upload (screenshots) plus arbitrary condition-specific data. For a test published as 'summary' and requested with public=true, entries are restricted to result, testName, testId, src and time. An unknown test id yields an empty array, not a 404.

BrowserDetail.description: Front-channel interaction state of a running test

show_qr_code.description: Whether the UI should render the URLs as QR codes (wallet tests)

urls.description: URLs the tester (or an automated browser) still needs to visit

urlsWithMethod.description: As 'urls', each with the HTTP method to use

browserApiRequests.description: Pending browser-API interactions, each with the request object and its submission URL

uriInputRequests.description: Pending requests for the tester to paste a URI, each with a submission URL and description

visitedUrlsWithMethod.description: As 'visited', each with the HTTP method used

runners.description: State of the automated browser runners processing the URLs

TestStatusResponse.description: Live state of a running test instance. Note this does not include the test's status or result — poll GET /api/info/{id} (or /api/runner/{id}/wait-state) for those.

exposed.description: Name-to-value strings the test exposes to the user (e.g. client_id)

created.description: When the test was created, ISO-8601

updated.description: When the test's status last changed, ISO-8601

error.description: Details of the test's final error, or null when there is none

browser.description: Front-channel interaction state; absent for tests without a browser component

ModuleEntry.description: One test module within a plan

variant.description: Module-specific variant values, if any (null otherwise)

instances.description: Ids of test instances already run for this module (empty at creation)

PlanCreatedResponse.description: Result of creating a test plan instance

name.description: The plan name that was requested

id.description: Id of the new test plan instance

modules.description: The test modules the plan will run, in order

ShareLinkResponse.description: A private link for sharing read-only access

link.description: Browser URL that logs a guest in via a one-time token

token.description: The JWT on its own, usable as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' on the read-only endpoints

message.description: Informational notice when the private-link signing key is not persistently configured; empty string otherwise

id.description: Id of the published test or plan

publish.description: The publication state that was set

CertificationPackageErrorResponse.description: Certification package could not be prepared because tests failed or are incomplete, the plan id is unknown, or the plan has no certification profile (it is not part of the certification program). Note: a 422 can also be returned with an empty body when the plan could not be marked immutable.

variant.description: The plan's variant selection, as a string

failed_tests.description: Per-module details of the failing or incomplete tests, keyed by module name; absent for the no_certification_profile error

FavoritePlansResponse.description: The current user's favorited plan names

plans.description: Plan names, in the order they were favorited

TokenSummary.description: An existing API token; the token value itself is never returned after creation

expires.description: Expiry time in milliseconds since the epoch, or null for a permanent token

WaitStateReached.description: The test reached one of the requested states

state.description: The status the test is now in

WaitStateTimeout.description: The wait timed out before the test reached any of the requested states

BrowserStatusResponse.description: Front-channel URL state for a running test (a subset of the 'browser' object returned by GET /api/runner/{id})

show_qr_code.description: Whether the UI should render the URLs as QR codes (wallet tests)

urls.description: URLs the tester (or an automated browser) still needs to visit

runners.description: State of the automated browser runners processing the URLs

draw.description: The 'draw' value from the request, echoed back

recordsTotal.description: Synthetic count, not a true total: start + length + 1 when a further page exists, otherwise start plus the number of records returned

recordsFiltered.description: Always the same value as recordsTotal (the suite does not compute a separate filtered count)

data.description: The page of records; the item type depends on the endpoint

TestInfoResponse.description: Stored information about one test instance. When requested with public=true the same shape is returned minus the 'config' field.

testId.description: Id of the test instance (same value as _id)

variant.description: Selected variant values (a plain name-to-value object; a bare string for pre-variant legacy tests)

started.description: When the test was created, ISO-8601

config.description: The test configuration JSON (absent when requested with public=true)

description.description: Free-text description from the configuration, or null

alias.description: Alias used in the test URLs, or null

planId.description: Id of the plan this test belongs to, or null for a standalone test

status.description: Current lifecycle status of the test

version.description: Conformance suite version that ran the test

summary.description: Summary line of the test module

result.description: Current result of the test, or null if not yet known

iss.description: Issuer of the user's login identity

sub.description: Subject of the user's login identity

principal.description: String rendering of the principal map (informational only; use iss/sub)

displayName.description: Display name from the login provider

isAdmin.description: Whether the user has the admin role

isGuest.description: True for a guest logged in via a private share link

bearerAuth.description: Either an API token from the token management page or a share-link JWT from a /share endpoint.
